items.summary: Matel Motion and Energy Solutions Private Limited has raised ₹130 crore from a Series B fundraise led by UC Impower, with Catamaran joining as a new investor and Transition VC continuing its support as an existing investor. Khaitan & Co advised Matel on this fundraise. The transaction team consisted of Bhavik Narsana (Partner), Shweta Dwivedi (Consultant), Pragya Mishra (Associate) and Sakshi Mehta (Associate). Bhavik Narsana JSA Advocates and Solicitors advised UC Impower Fund, the lead investor, and Catamaran Ventures on this fundraise. The Firm assisted UC Impower on all aspects of the transaction, including advising on the term sheet, conducting legal due diligence on Matel, negotiating and finalising the definitive documents, and advising on pre-closing and closing actions. JSA also provided end-to-end transaction support to Catamaran, advising on the term sheet, negotiating definitive documents, and assisting until closing. The transaction team advising UC Impower Fund was led by Gerald Manoharan (Partner) and Manuel Jose (Partner), with support from Harshita Agarwal (Senior Associate) and Shobika Veluprakash (Associate). items.title: State tells Supreme Court Shyamkanu Mahanta pressured Zubeen Garg to go to Singapore; arranged women, alcohol
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the State of Assam to diligently proceed with the trial against Northeast Festival organiser Shyamkanu Mahanta, an accused in the case concerning the drowning death of renowned Assamese singer Zubeen Garg. [Shyamkanu Mahanta v. State of Assam] A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and R Mahadevan passed the direction while hearing a bail plea filed by Mahanta. Mahanta, who has organised the Northeast Festival since 2013, was arrested after Garg died while swimming in Singapore on September 19, 2025 Today, Advocate General (AG) Devajit Saikia , representing the State of Assam, told the Court that the trial was proceeding on a day-to-day basis and that crucial witnesses were likely to be examined over the next few weeks. “ The prosecution shall be diligent in prosecuting this case, ” the Court ordered. Justice Nagarathna orally remarked that the Court was putting pressure on the State to proceed with the trial and would examine the progress made when the matter is heard next.
